name: Seared Sirloin Steak with White Wine Gravy
method: skillet (sear whole-muscle sirloin steaks, build a roux-based white-wine beef gravy in the same pan, simmer to finish; batch-scales by searing in batches and making the gravy in a pot, weigh-and-divide steak + gravy over a low-carb side)
ingredients_verbatim: 2 lbs. top sirloin steak, or strip steak or ribeye
2-3 drops gravy master or kitchen bouquet (optional)
unmapped: mustard powder (board carries prepared mustard/dijon-mustard, not dry mustard powder)
ground sage (board carries fresh-sage, not ground sage; poultry-seasoning is the nearest)
gravy master / kitchen bouquet (optional browning liquid, no board home)
why: Verified full-dish published nutrition sits dead-center in the band: 490 cal, 8 g carbs, and a standout 53 g protein per serving. Whole-muscle top sirloin, seared then simmered in a roux-and-white-wine beef gravy - squarely in the roast/steak lane, not ground and not a slow-braise. Structurally low-carb (only the flour roux + a little brown sugar contribute carbs, no rice/potato/bread base), so our label-accurate recompute has wide headroom under the 35 g ceiling. Distinct from the catalog's ground salisbury steaks and the cubed beef-tips-and-gravy-over-rice entry: this is whole seared steak in a wine gravy. Nearly every ingredient maps to the Omaha board (sirloin-steak, butter, white-wine, beef-broth, flour, worcestershire, the spice rack); the three flagged items are minor optional/dry seasonings that exercise the pricer's unmapped queue.
confidence: high on nutrition (read directly from the source recipe card); note mild dup-adjacency to the live beef-tips-and-gravy entry, but cut form (whole steak vs tips) and sauce (white-wine gravy) differ.
